newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MOZAMBIQUE IRON PLANT VITAL FOR JCI FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: MOZAMBIQUE IRON PLANT VITAL FOR JCI FUTURE.

text.p: South African mining house JCI Ltd saw the development of a planned $662 million iron ore reduction plant in Mozambique as vital to the company's future plans to compete in the global commodity market.
JCI chairman Mzi Khumalo was quoted by South African newspapers on Wednesday as saying the project -- first announced in November last year -- would be central to economic development in Mozambique.
The $662 million project is planned to be erected north of the Mozambican port of Beira and aims to produce 2.5 million tonnes of hot briquetted iron (HBI) for export mainly to the Far East.
"This is the first in a series of plans to expand JCI's participation in the global commodities market and help it to become a global multi-commodity company.
"And it will be one of the most competitive merchant iron projects in the world," Business Report quoted Khumalo as saying.
The project's viability was enhanced by low-cost gas which would be supplied from Mozambique's Temane and Buzi gas fields at less than $0.75 a gigajoule, JCI said in a briefing document.
"The justification for this project is the low cost natural gas available close to the port of Beira," JCI said.
Atlantic Richfield Co (Arco) is developing the Temane gas field while Leopardus Resources Ltd and Scimitar Hydrocarbons Corp were jointly exploring the Buzi gas field.

"The gas will be sold over the fence to JCI Ltd by the Arco/Leopardus team on an intergrated net back formula ensuring that the cost of the reductant will be one of the lowest in the world," JCI said.
A feasibility study would be completed by the end of 1997 while a decision to go ahead could be taken early next year.
Provided approval is granted for the project, construction could begin in early 1998 and the plant could produce its first iron in 2001.
JCI holds a 52 percent stake in the project, the Mozambique government 20 percent, the Zimbabwean government three percent and other partners 25 percent.
